title: Finite cohomological amplitude from bounds on cohomology objects
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian] with derived categories $D(\mathcal A),D(\mathcal B)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], standard cohomology functors $H^i$ and shift convention $H^i(M[r])=H^{i+r}(M)$. Let $T:D(\mathcal A)	o D(\mathcal B)$ be an exact triangulated functor (with its shift comparisons) [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Let $\mathcal S$ be a class of objects of $\mathcal A$, closed under isomorphism and containing zero, and let $c\leq d$ be integers. Suppose that for every $M\in\mathcal S$, viewed as $M[0]$, one has $H^i(T(M[0]))=0$ for $i
otin[c,d]$. Then for every pair of integers $a\leq b$ and every $K\in D(\mathcal A)$ with $H^r(K)=0$ for $r
otin[a,b]$ and $H^r(K)\in\mathcal S$ for all $r$, one has
$$H^i(TK)=0\qquad(i
otin[a+c,b+d]).$$
No product-preservation or completeness assumption on $T$ or on either derived category is required.

source.place: Tag 08J5, remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle: finite induction on the successive cohomology triangles. The same bounded-input argument is used in more-etale.tex Tag 0G2A, lemma-derived-lower-shriek-bounded, proof of (3).

proof.text: Choose a representative complex C of K using essential surjectivity of Q. Transport the vanishing hypotheses and membership in S along the homologyFunctorFactors isomorphisms. Thus C.IsGE a and C.IsLE b by Mathlib CochainComplex.isGE_iff and isLE_iff. Put K_q=Q(tau_{<=q}C). Induct on natural n with a-1+n<=b to bound T(K_{a-1+n}) in the fixed interval [a+c,b+d]. No limit is used.

source.place: Tag 08J5, remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle; canonical truncation cohomology as in homology.tex Section 0118

proof.text: For $a\le q\le b$, the hypothesis applies to $H^q(K)\in\mathcal S$. The shift comparison of the exact functor and [lem-sp-derived-cohomology-shift] give $T(H^q(K)[-q])\cong T(H^q(K)[0])[-q]$ and hence $H^i(T(H^q(K)[-q]))\cong H^{i-q}(T(H^q(K)[0]))$. This is zero for $i<q+c$ or $i>q+d$. Since $a+c\le q+c$ and $q+d\le b+d$, it is in particular zero whenever $i\notin[a+c,b+d]$. The sign is $i-q$, in accordance with the stipulated convention $H^i(M[r])=H^{i+r}(M)$.

source.place: Tag 08J5, successive cohomology object H^q(K)[-q]; shifts as in homology.tex Tags 011G and 011H

proof.text: For n=0, the bounded-below clause of [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle] gives (tau_{<=a-1}C).IsGE a. Canonical truncation also gives IsLE (a-1), so Mathlib DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.isZero shows that K_{a-1} is zero. Exactness of T implies additivity and preservation of zero objects. Applying T and H^i therefore gives the base case.

source.place: Tag 05RU, definition-unbounded-derived-category; Tag 08J5, start of finite truncation induction

proof.text: For the induction step, suppose $0\le n<b-a+1$ and set $q=a+n$, so $a\le q\le b$. The induction hypothesis bounds $T K_{q-1}$. Apply $T$ to the distinguished triangle $K_{q-1}\to K_q\to H^q(K)[-q]\to K_{q-1}[1]$ of [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle]; it is still distinguished because $T$ is exact. By [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact], for each $i$ the segment $H^i(T K_{q-1})\to H^i(T K_q)\to H^i(T(H^q(K)[-q]))$ is exact. If $i\notin[a+c,b+d]$, its first term is zero by induction and its third term is zero by Step 2. Exactness then forces the middle term to be zero: its kernel for the map to zero is the whole middle object and equals the zero image of the preceding map. This proves the claim for $n+1$.

source.place: Tag 08J5, remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle, second displayed triangle; finite induction also explicit in more-etale.tex Tag 0G2A, lemma-derived-lower-shriek-bounded, proof of (3)

proof.text: At n=(b-a+1).toNat the truncation index is b, so the induction bounds T(K_b). Since C.IsLE b, Mathlib CochainComplex.quasiIso_ιTruncLE_iff makes tau_{<=b}C -> C a quasi-isomorphism. Q inverts it. Compose its image with Q(C) ≅ K and apply T and H^i to transport the bound. The construction uses neither infinite products nor completeness.
